h: Plan the Route, Save Your Legs
p: Marwell is big, and a bit of planning makes a real difference. Grab a map when you arrive, decide which zones matter most to your crew and work out a loop rather than criss-crossing the site. Little ones will want the lemurs and the penguins, older kids will be hunting the snow leopards and the reptiles, and everyone will want to see the giraffes. Factor in breaks at the playgrounds and you'll find the hours fly by.

Keeper talks are scattered through the day and they're well worth timing your route around, because hearing the stories behind the animals brings the whole place to life. With so much ground to cover, it's worth bringing a refillable bottle and snacks, plus a picnic blanket in summer. A light waterproof is wise most of the year, as Hampshire showers have a habit of popping up out of nowhere.

Winchester and its surroundings are packed with things to do. Winchester Science Centre, on the edge of the city, has hands-on exhibits and a planetarium, which is great for a rainy afternoon. In town, the remains of Wolvesey Castle, once a palace of the bishops of Winchester, sit near the cathedral, and the bronze statue of King Alfred stands proudly at the end of The Broadway. A short drive away, the Watercress Line runs heritage steam trains from Alresford, and Sir Harold Hillier Gardens at Ampfield is a beautiful spot for a stroll among trees and flowers. Put together, that's a cracking long weekend in Hampshire.
